The centralizer of a subset $A \subseteq G$ is defined as
$$C_G(A) = \{g \in G \mid ga = ag \text{ for all } a \in A\}.$$
We prove that this equals $\{g \in G \mid g^{-1}ag = a \text{ for all } a \in A\}$.

**Proof.** We show the two defining conditions are equivalent for any $g \in G$ and $a \in A$.

($\Rightarrow$) Suppose $ga = ag$. Left-multiply both sides by $g^{-1}$:
$$g^{-1}(ga) = g^{-1}(ag) \implies (g^{-1}g)a = g^{-1}a(g) \implies e\,a = g^{-1}ag \implies a = g^{-1}ag.$$

($\Leftarrow$) Suppose $g^{-1}ag = a$. Left-multiply both sides by $g$:
$$g(g^{-1}ag) = g\,a \implies (gg^{-1})(ag) = ga \implies e(ag) = ga \implies ag = ga.$$

Hence for every $g \in G$:
$$\bigl(\forall a \in A:\; ga = ag\bigr) \iff \bigl(\forall a \in A:\; g^{-1}ag = a\bigr).$$

Therefore the two sets are equal:
$$C_G(A) = \{g \in G \mid ga = ag \text{ for all } a \in A\} = \{g \in G \mid g^{-1}ag = a \text{ for all } a \in A\}. \qquad \blacksquare$$
